## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening

**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
checks as human code (S10).

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). `GITHUB_TOKEN` "restricted" by default, `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
  deploys may still need a stored credential: a proposed time-boxed exception to S2 = 0 (Q1).
- **Side paths:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard providers reach AWS
  (📖 R4.4.9) outside the GitHub gate (⚠️ R4.4.9); not used for prod (⚠️ R4.6 #6).
- **Pinning:** workflow lockfile (`gh actions-lock`) or full SHA, enforced by the org policy "Require
  actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA"; the lockfile does not pin reusable workflows, so
  the deploy workflow lives in the same repo (📖 R3.5.5).
- **CODEOWNERS** on `.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`,
  `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc` (📖 R3.2.8; list ⚠️ R6.5 #5); CI validates the file, because
  invalid lines are skipped silently (📖 R3.2.7).
- **No privileged triggers with untrusted code** (`pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` + checkout,
  📖 R3.5.4).
- **Agents in CI:** `claude-code-action` with a custom GitHub App limited to Contents, Issues, Pull
  requests (📖 R1.7.8); Anthropic workload identity federation, not a personal OAuth token (📖 R1.7.6);
  `--restricted` and explicit `--tools` (D3; passing it through `claude_args` unverified, ⚠️ research
  6.9.4 Q5); a managed-settings file on the runner, which also guards against mods (📖 R1.5.6; for
  federation auth ⚠️); MCP set fixed by CI because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
  (📖 R1.3.5); never `environment: production` (⚠️ R3.6 #4). Hosted runners give `sudo` (📖 R3.5.1),
  so with `Bash` in `--tools` the runner file is advisory (⚠️ R3.5.1, R3.6 #4).
- **App-opened PRs:** a required check with a pinned source app confirms at least one approval by a
  human who did not trigger the run; counting approvals is not enough, since the app's own approval
  might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3; 📖 R3.2.5).
- **Required checks (S10):** secret scanning, dependency check, SAST (products: G4); IAM Access
  Analyzer `check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1); Pulumi policy packs (📖 R4.2.2).

**Audit evidence.** Workflows and lockfile in git; audit-log events such as
`org.update_actions_secret`, `repo.set_workflow_permission_can_approve_pr`, `repository_ruleset.update`
(📖 R3.3.3, R3.5.6); check results per PR; secrets inventory (S2).

**Cost / value.** One-time migration to OIDC and pinned actions; slower action updates. Compliance
gets S2 and the same guardrails for agent and human code.

## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence

**Principle.** PHI never reaches the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9). Other customer
personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved,
tenant-scoped, time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic (GĐ-14).

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Paths to PHI** (research 1.11.4 lists 17):
  - AWS stores: closed by identity, through `ProdReadMetadata` from phase 1 and the SCP from phase 2
    (layer 1); no Aurora credentials, no prod exec, no `lambda:InvokeFunction` for agent-usable roles
    [design; actions ⚠️ G13];
  - k0s logs/exec and GCP stores (L1, L11, L13): same principle, mechanism open (G1, G3);
  - tickets/chat via MCP, pasted text, internal admin pages, prod AI traces, fixtures, CI logs (L5,
    L8–L10, L12, L14): process and hygiene only;
  - logs redacted at source with raw payloads in a separate log group; alerts carry IDs, not payloads [design].
- **Real-data request** [design]: tenant, purpose, store, window, agreement; approved by the data owner
  and an approver ≠ requester; JIT data-read role, 1 h. Per-tenant scoping through session tags
  (📖 R2.1.8) is unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️).
  - **PHI:** a human reads in a terminal without an agent; the agent gets a redacted summary. This
    narrows GĐ-9 because the agent stays outside PHI scope (research 1.9) and Team is not shown as
    BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Enterprise + BAA only for a separate environment if needed (research 1.9).
  - **Non-PHI personal data:** the agent may read it within the approved request (GĐ-9).
- **Partner-uploaded claim documents (A7b):** never in an agent session raw; reproduce with synthetic
  documents, or de-identify first [design]. The document is PHI and an injection vector (research
  1.11.4 L6).
- **Injection** (these lower frequency; layers 1 and 3 limit impact): Manual by default; the auto-mode
  classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions (📖 R6.3.5). Broad allowed domains such as
  `github.com` are a documented exfiltration path (📖 R6.3.7). The incident session has no edit tools
  and runs outside the repo, but its Bash can still write locally and send data out through excluded
  commands (layer 2); what is at stake is bounded by "no standing write, no PHI read". Shared knowledge
  goes in `CLAUDE.md` under review; auto memory is unprotected unless `--restricted` (📖 R6.3.11, D3).
- **Tenants:** one tenant per data-read grant; a session that read one tenant's data does not post to
  shared places without review (⚠️ R6.5 #8, process). Logical separation in shared accounts is assumed
  (GĐ-3).
- **Non-prod:** no prod copies (S11). A scan of non-prod stores runs at the start of phase 1 (tool:
  G4); a store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule (GĐ-14). Cost: until scanned, that store is
  not part of the free loop.
- **Local stores:** transcripts and memory hold what the agent read (research 1.11.4); set
  `cleanupPeriodDays` (30 in the HIPAA sample, 📖 R5.5.4; what it deletes ⚠️).
- **Cross-border (Vietnam example):** processing data collected in Vietnam on a platform abroad is a
  transfer (📖 R5.4.5); agent flows, including employee names in logs and transcripts, update the
  transfer impact assessment (⚠️ R5.7 #4, needs Papaya legal).

**Audit evidence.** SCP/IAM text as the written access rule for sensitive data (📖 R5.4.3; ⚠️ R5.7 #5);
data-read requests and the data-read role's CloudTrail; planted-injection reports (layer 8); non-prod
scan results (S11).

**Cost / value.** Debugging with redacted and synthetic data; a request for the rare real-data read.
Compliance gets "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM, and a record per exception (S9).

## Layer 7 — Observability, audit, incident response and break-glass

**Principle.** One tamper-evident evidence chain per prod change. One routed alert channel with a
named on-call, approvers included. Unapproved change is detected (drift, reconciliation). Break-glass
is approved before use, time-boxed and reconciled after.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Audit stores:**
  - organization CloudTrail to a log-archive account with integrity validation (📖 R2.6.2, R2.6.4,
    R2.6.5); change records ≥ 6 years; raw-log retention for Papaya's compliance owner (⚠️ R5.7 #2).
    Data events only on PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS (📖 R2.6.3), which makes the archive
    PHI-bearing (⚠️ research 1.11.4 L15). CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers (📖 R2.6.6);
  - GitHub org audit log kept 180 days, so exported (📖 R3.5.6);
  - alerts on `repository_ruleset.update`, `environment.update_protection_rule`,
    `environment.remove_protection_rule`, `environment.delete`, `protected_branch.policy_override`
    (📖 R3.5.6, R3.1.4; selection ⚠️ R3.6 #1). UI changes to the branch policy may leave no event, and a
    deleted `production` environment comes back unprotected (⚠️ R3.1.4): a job compares live settings
    with an expected copy (G8);
  - Aurora SQL is likely invisible to CloudTrail (⚠️ R2.7.1): Database Activity Streams, alerts on
    lost-record events, stream treated as PHI (📖 R2.7.2; Serverless v2 ⚠️);
  - Claude Code OTel without prompt content (layer 2).
- **Change record [design]:** keyed by commit SHA or JIT request ID; links PR, approvals, run ID,
  preview and CloudTrail events. Monthly reconciliation: every prod write event matches a record
  approved before apply (S3). Actor: `onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name plus
  directory lookup (📖 R2.5.1; ⚠️ R2.5.3).
- **Drift [design]:** its own read role, trusted only from a `drift` environment on `main`; it can read
  prod secrets in state, which is noted (⚠️ R4.6 #2). Scheduled `pulumi preview --refresh
  --expect-no-changes` or `pulumi refresh --preview-only` (📖 R4.1.1, R4.3.1, R4.3.2); CloudFormation
  drift detection, explicitly set properties only (📖 R4.4.6). No auto-remediation: it is an unreviewed
  `pulumi up --refresh` (📖 R4.3.2). Each finding gets an actor and a ticket.
- **On-call:** phase 1 delivers only the named approver schedule (primary + backup, 24/7), as decided
  in framing round 1, including a platform approver because L3 needs one (Options §1). Alert routing and
  the rest of on-call follow in phase 2 (tools: G5).
- **Break-glass = JIT fallback** [design unless marked]:

  | Step | Rule |
  |---|---|
  | When | The PR path cannot be used: operation not in IaC and no runbook; GitHub/Actions down; pipeline broken. The approver refuses JIT for anything expressible in IaC while the pipeline works, and records why. |
  | Request | Command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub. |
  | Approval | On-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant. |
  | Grant | `InfraOperator-<service>`, 1 h (📖 R2.1.4). Deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3); ending the portal session does not end role sessions (📖 R2.4.3); an immediate stop needs the revocation SCP (📖 R2.4.4). |
  | Execution | The human types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). |
  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |

  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, `claims-doc-extract`, Actions outage. Run
  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."

  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %). On a breach,
  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
  (D2, ⚠️).

**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail; exported GitHub audit log; change records and monthly
reconciliation (S3, S8 ≤ 30 min); JIT requests, reconciliations, codify PRs; drift tickets; on-call
schedule and approval waits (S7).

**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
incidents, plus detection.

---

## Layer 8 — Governance and rollout

**Principle.** Every control has an owner, a metric and a review date. Policies are files changed by
PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
attacks.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Owners:** DevSecOps (framework, managed settings, catalogue, metrics); platform team (deploy
  workflows, rulesets, pipelines); Compliance (evidence review, supplier register, Statement of
  Applicability); engineering leads (CODEOWNERS); engineering management (on-call schedule).
- **Policy as code:** managed settings, catalogue, SCPs, trust policies, CODEOWNERS and workflows are
  files under CODEOWNERS; GitHub settings that are not files are compared with an expected copy
  (⚠️ R3.6 #1; G8). Few GitHub admins, reviewed quarterly.
- **Metrics:** S1–S11 exactly as in framing §5; this framework adds the JIT metrics (layer 7) and the
  prompt metrics (layer 2). S2 and S5 have caveats (Q1; layer 2).
- **Rollout** (≈ 90 days, GĐ-12 unconfirmed). Framing round 1 Q8: (1) remove long-lived CI credentials,
  (2) narrow standing prod access, (3) MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list before or with (2).

  | Phase | Days | Items, in order |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | 0–30 | Measure the incident PR lane on one service (first task, Options §9). Non-prod data scan. OIDC for deploy workflows; remove long-lived keys; move laptop deploys (GĐ-10) to CI. Rulesets and CODEOWNERS. `ProdReadMetadata`; start moving secrets to runtime resolution. On-call approver schedule and minimal JIT fallback, **then** remove standing prod write. MCP/plugin catalogue v1. Managed settings baseline. Start verifying the SSM option (Options §7). The last two may slip to phase 2 if the 1–2 person team (GĐ-1) runs short. |
  | 2 | 30–60 | SCP data-plane deny; drift detection; audit-log export, change records, reconciliation; Aurora activity streams; JIT reconciliation job; alert routing and the rest of on-call. |
  | 3 | 60–90 | Planted-injection test on the real configuration (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.5; ⚠️ R6.5 #12); auto-mode non-prod environment (D1 c); separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions; first ISO evidence pack; 90-day review of D1–D3. |

- **Exceptions:** a ticket with owner, reason and expiry.
- **Standards mapping** (⚠️ R5.6; HIPAA and Vietnam text 📖 R5.2, R5.4; ISO IDs recalled, not read,
  ⚠️ R5.1):

  | Layers | ISO 27001:2022 Annex A (⚠️) | HIPAA Security Rule | Vietnam example |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1, 6 access | 5.15–5.18, 8.2, 8.3, 8.5 | 164.312(a)(2)(i); 164.308(a)(3)–(4) | Decree 356 Art. 4(2) |
  | 3, 5 change | 8.32, 8.31, 8.25, 5.3 | 164.312(c); 164.316(b) | — |
  | 7 logging, break-glass | 8.15, 8.16, 5.28 | 164.312(b); 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D); 164.312(a)(2)(ii) (mapping ⚠️ R5.7 #3) | Law 91 Art. 23 (72 h notice) |
  | 4 suppliers | 5.19–5.23 | 164.308(b), 164.314(a) | Law 91 Art. 20 |

  "A named human approves" is Papaya's chosen way to meet these controls, not a literal requirement
  (⚠️ R5.7 #1).
- **Out of scope:** security of the production AI agents (A7a); noted as a follow-up.

**Audit evidence.** Git history of policy files; monthly metrics; 90-day review minutes; exception
register; planted-injection reports.

**Cost / value.** Steady, small overhead for DevSecOps and platform. Compliance gets a managed system
with owners and review dates.

---

## Gaps (not covered by `work/02-research.md`)

| # | Gap | Layers |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | k0s: authentication, RBAC, audit logging, kubeconfig issuance (GĐ-4) | 1, 3, 6 |
| G2 | Firebase Hosting deploy from CI without a stored token | 1, 5 |

| G7 | GitHub Actions log and artifact retention, and export | 3, 7 |
| G8 | Rulesets and environment settings through the API | 7, 8 |
| G9 | How Linear and Slack MCP servers authenticate | 4, 6 |
| G10 | OIDC subject customisation (`job_workflow_ref`) on GitHub Team | 1 |
| G11 | Closing provider/login bypasses on laptops without MDM | 2 |
| G12 | `pulumi up` flag reference for the prod allowlist | 3 |
| G13 | IAM actions for every data-plane read (S3, SQS, Step Functions, Secrets Manager, RDS, ECS Exec, Lambda invoke) | 1, 6 |

## Owner questions (defaults chosen in this draft)

| # | Question | Default in this draft |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Accept a time-boxed exception to S2 = 0 for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials until G1/G2 are solved? | Yes, with owner and expiry in the exception register. |

# Framework: coding agents for DevSecOps at Papaya

> Status: draft v3, for owner review · Updated: 2026-11-09
> Audience: a panel of Engineering and Compliance. Each layer ends with what it costs engineers and
> what it gives Compliance.

## How to read this

Eight layers. Each has a **Principle** (tool-independent), **On Papaya's stack** (Pulumi,
Serverless Framework, GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, k0s, Claude Code) and **Audit evidence** (records an
auditor can test without asking anyone). Copy-paste detail belongs in `examples/`.

| Marker | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 📖 R*x.y* | Documented. R*x.y* is a ✅/📖 row in `work/02-research.md` that quotes and links the official page. |
| ⚠️ R*x.y* | Inference, open question or "What this means for Papaya" conclusion in the research (sections 1.8, 2.9, 3.6, 3.7, 4.6, 5.6, 5.7, 6.5). Reasoned, not documented. |
| ⚠️ | Not verified at all, e.g. an illustrative command. |
| [design] | My proposal, built from documented parts, untested. Treat as ⚠️. |

Nothing here was checked locally (✅): this is a design without access to Papaya's systems.
**GĐ-n** = owner-confirmed assumption in `work/01-problem-framing.md` §4; **S-n** = success criteria
(§5); **P/A-n** = problems (§1); **D1–D3** = owner decisions in research 6.6; **Options §n** =
`work/03-options.md`; **G-n** = gaps; **Q-n** = owner questions (both at the end).

---

## 1. The decision in one page

Engineering and Compliance disagree only about **writes to production**; reads of metadata and all
of non-prod are outside Compliance's sentence (framing §3.1). Real customer data is layer 6.

**Chosen approach "A + D2'"** (Options §9, owner decision 2026-11-09):

1. **Default path:** every prod change is a pull request, approved by a named human who is not the
   author, applied by CI. Incidents included ("IaC first").
2. **Fallback (break-glass):** only when the PR path cannot be used, a human gets a 1-hour approved
   grant and runs an approved command list in a terminal without an agent (layer 7) [design].
3. **Nothing standing:** no human or agent holds standing prod write; no long-lived credentials.

| Engineering gets | Compliance gets |
|---|---|
| A free loop in non-prod: read, change, deploy without approval (non-prod is synthetic, GĐ-14). | Every prod change approved **before** apply by a named human ≠ author (GĐ-8, GĐ-11), enforced in GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent. |
| Read-only prod metadata for the agent. | No standing prod write (S1), no long-lived CI keys (S2). |
| Self-service PRs, one approval, same-day ship (S4). | One evidence chain per change; approval and change records ≥ 6 years (📖 R5.2.9; applied to change records ⚠️ R5.7 #2). |
| Incident lane: approval wait ≤ 15 min, 24/7 (S7). Decision-to-apply target ≤ 30 min (Options §9); current estimate 11–46 min ⚠️, measured first in rollout. | Agent-side controls as a second layer, not the control of record. |

**Where the design falls short, stated openly:**

- **The fallback meets the approval rule only partly** (approves a command list, not an applied
  change); accepted by the owner (Options §9 Q2). It is a second, process-controlled path, while the
  framing asked for one technically enforced path (framing §3.3, Options §7). It stays narrow only
  if most incidents are expressible in IaC (unknown, Options §8); layer 7 measures this.
- **On GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before apply** (⚠️ R4.6 #1; Team assumed, GĐ-5).
  Risky prod diffs stop the deploy for a second approval [design].
- **Admins can edit the gate**; logged, not prevented (📖 R3.2.2, ⚠️ R3.6 #1). An admin's agent has
  the same power, because the agent uses its engineer's GitHub login.
- **Some rules are process, not technology:** see "Process rules" in layer 1.
- **HIPAA applicability is a legal question** (⚠️ R1.11.1.11); the design treats Papaya as a
  business associate, as the brief implies.

**Cross-cutting rules** (owner's balance principle, research 6.8):

1. **The boundary is IAM and the CI gate.** Server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not
   a security boundary" (📖 R1.1.7); local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8).
2. **Assume prompt injection succeeds:** OWASP and NIST state there is no full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
3. **Friction where damage is large, none where it is small**, measured, with a time-boxed escape.
4. **Evidence by construction:** the path produces the records.

### Roles

| Role | Rule |
|---|---|
| Author (engineer + their agent) | Never approves own change; GitHub blocks PR authors from approving (📖 R3.3.1). |
| Approver | Named human in CODEOWNERS; ≠ author, ≠ last pusher (📖 R3.2.3); for an app-opened PR, ≠ the person who triggered it (⚠️ R3.3.4, layer 5). |
| On-call approver | Primary + backup, 24/7, on the on-call schedule; wait ≤ 15 min (S7). |
| Platform approver [design] | Platform-team member, also on call; one of the two approvers for L3. |
| Data owner [design] | Named per tenant; co-approves real-data reads (layer 6). |
| Control owner | DevSecOps (1–2 people, GĐ-1); owns policies and metrics; not the only approver. |

---

## Layer 1 — Identity and access

**Principle.** Every action traces to one named human. Nobody holds standing prod write: prod is
written by the pipeline role, or in the fallback by an approved, time-boxed grant. Prod reads default
to metadata. No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **The engineer's access is the agent's access.** The agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and
  one portal session reaches every role assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2). A separate
  "agent" permission set does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is what the **engineer**
  holds.
- **Process rules** that follow from this (owner accepted them as process controls, D2, D3):
  - the JIT terminal and the real-data terminal run no agent, though the grant is reachable from the
    same laptop;
  - the incident-analysis session is meant to use only read-only roles;
  - an agent does not approve PRs. GitHub blocks self-approval only. The auto-mode default block list
    names "approving Claude's own pull request", not approving someone else's (📖 R6.3.3), and it
    applies only in auto mode. No detection was found (⚠️; `actor_is_agent` in the audit log has no
    documented meaning, R3.5.6).
- **IAM Identity Center permission sets** (📖 R2.1.1) [design names]:
  - `ProdReadMetadata`: metrics, redacted log groups, configuration; no data-plane read on claim
    stores; 1 h session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). Lambda configuration can hold secrets resolved by
    Serverless in plain text (⚠️ R4.4.7), so configuration reads are allowed per service only after
    its secrets move to runtime resolution (⚠️ R4.6 #7). Cost: until then the agent reads
    timeout/memory from the IaC code;
  - `NonProdDeveloper`: broad, non-prod accounts only;
  - `InfraOperator-<service>`: assigned only by the JIT flow (layer 7), via a partner product, the
    TEAM sample or a small flow on `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment`
    (📖 R2.4.1, R2.4.1b, R2.4.2);
  - no standing prod-write permission set.
- **SCPs on the prod OU** [design] (SCPs cap member-account principals, 📖 R2.3.1, R2.3.2):
  - deny data-plane reads on claim stores except application roles and the approved data-read role,
    by `aws:PrincipalArn` (📖 R2.3.8; pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4). Actions, e.g. `s3:GetObject`,
    `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`, are incomplete and unchecked (⚠️ G13);
  - deny `lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` / `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` (⚠️ R4.6 #3) except
    CloudFormation `deploymentRole`s, the Pulumi prod deploy role (if Pulumi manages Lambdas) and the
    JIT roles. This closes `serverless deploy function`, which changes config outside CloudFormation
    (📖 R4.4.4), and needs `deploymentRole` set on every Serverless stack (📖 R4.4.5);
  - a pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:userId` (📖 R2.4.4); protect the org trail (📖 R2.6.2).
  - Limits: 10 SCPs per target, 10,240 characters; no SCP applies to the management account
    (📖 R2.3.2, R2.3.4), so whatever deploys SCPs there is the most sensitive role (L3 path).
- **Sessions/MFA:** portal session length set on purpose; an IdP session can extend it silently
  (📖 R2.1.5, R2.1.6). MFA lives in the external IdP if one is used (📖 R2.1.7).
- **CI → AWS:** GitHub OIDC, no stored keys (📖 R3.4.1). The prod role trusts only the `production`
  environment of the monorepo, in its `sub` format (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4; immutable format assumed,
  ⚠️ R3.7 A2), ideally customised with the deploy workflow's `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
- **CI → GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization, which Google
  requires (📖 R3.4.5b).
- **k0s, GCP and Firebase for humans:** same principles; mechanisms not researched (G1–G3). Today
  k0s is reached with kubeconfigs, no SSO (GĐ-4, unconfirmed). Interim: no admin kubeconfig and no GCP
  owner role on laptops; prod deploys only from CI. Firebase is not on the GCP BAA list (📖 R5.5.3), so
  Firebase Hosting must hold no PHI (⚠️ R5.7 #7).

**Audit evidence.** Identity Center assignment export (S1); CloudTrail `CreateAccountAssignment` /
`DeleteAccountAssignment` per grant (📖 R2.4.2), linked to its approval by request ID [design]; SCPs
and trust policies as Pulumi code; IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on policy PRs
(📖 R2.8.1); quarterly access review of permission sets and GitHub admins.

**Cost / value.** Engineers lose standing prod write, keep fast prod reads and a free non-prod loop.
Compliance gets least privilege that is enforced.

---

## Layer 2 — Agent runtime controls

**Principle.** Agent-side controls are hygiene, not the boundary. They are central, versioned in git
and the same for everyone. Defaults are safe; overrides are measured. The session that reads
untrusted content holds as little power as possible (📖 R6.1.2).

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Delivery:** server-managed settings (available on Team, 📖 R1.1.5) for all laptops. With MDM, also
  an endpoint file; by default one managed source supplies most keys, so the two must carry the same
  keys or use `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"` (📖 R1.1.3, R1.1.4). MDM is unknown; both are prepared.
- **Baseline** (template: Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json`, 📖 R5.5.4). All keys 📖 at the row cited:

  | Key | Value and reason |
  |---|---|
  | `permissions.defaultMode` | `default` (Manual). A default, not a lock: users can switch to auto; VS Code remembers the last pick (D1, R6.9.3). |
  | `permissions.allow` | Read-only commands Papaya uses, to cut prompts (R6.9.3). |
  | `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` | `true`, one rule set (D1, owner Q4; R1.2.5). Cost: project and user rules are ignored, so the managed set must carry every deny/ask rule projects need; prompts likely rise (⚠️ research 6.9.4 Q4). |
  | `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` | `"disable"`: removes "prompts off" (P3a; R1.2.2). Auto mode stays available (D1). |
  | `permissions.deny` / `ask` | Deny credential paths (R5.5.4; `Read(...)` syntax ⚠️ R1.8 #5). Ask for `WebFetch`, which the sandbox domain list does not limit (R1.6.2); cost: a prompt per fetch. |
  | `requiredMinimumVersion` | ≥ 2.1.295 (`onFailure: "block"`, R1.5.2) and ≥ the latest fixed advisory at rollout (R6.3.9). It does not end running sessions and fails open on a bad value (R1.1.13). |
  | `allowedProviders` + `forceLoginOrgUUID` | `["anthropic"]` + Papaya's org; closes most bypasses on **endpoint-managed** machines (R1.1.15). |
  | `allowManagedHooksOnly` | `true` (R1.5.4). |
  | sandbox | `sandbox.enabled`, `failIfUnavailable`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`, narrow `network.allowedDomains` locked by `network.allowManagedDomainsOnly` (R1.6.4); `credentials` / `filesystem.denyRead` on `~/.aws` (R1.6.3). |
  | MCP, plugins | Layer 4. |
  | OTel | Exporter on, content flags `0` (R1.1.20, R5.5.4). |

- **Trade-off on AWS credentials.** With `~/.aws` hidden from the sandbox, `aws`, `pulumi` and
  `serverless` must be `sandbox.excludedCommands`, which run "with full access", network included
  (📖 R1.6.4). So these tools are an egress channel outside the allowlist. Accepted because the
  engineer holds no prod write and no PHI read; the deny still stops other programs from taking the
  credentials. Stronger option, phase 3: a separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions
  (⚠️ R6.5 #2).
- **Session types:**

  | Session | Identity | Flags | Enforcement |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Daily development (laptop) | non-prod roles + `ProdReadMetadata` | baseline | Auto mode by choice (D1); `--restricted` recommended (D3). |
  | Incident analysis (laptop) | meant to be `ProdReadMetadata` only | `--restricted --tools "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob"`, started in an empty scratch directory, not the repo [design] | Process rule (D3, owner Q1–Q2). No Edit/Write/WebFetch (📖 R6.9.1b), but Bash can still write in its working directory (📖 R1.6.3) and call any role in the cache. |
  | CI agent (hosted runner) | own GitHub App token; never `production` | `--restricted`, explicit `--tools`; all rules in a managed-settings file on the runner | Workflow file under CODEOWNERS (D3, owner Q5). The file is advisory if `Bash` is in `--tools` (layer 5). |
  | JIT terminal | JIT grant | no agent | Process rule (D2). |
  | Auto-mode environment (phase 3) | non-prod only | auto encouraged | D1 option (c). |

- **Hard limits:** Bash rules are not a boundary (📖 R1.2.6); hooks fail open unless
  `"onFailure": "block"` (📖 R1.5.2); `--restricted` cannot be forced on laptops (📖 R6.9.1, R6.9.1c);
  on laptops **without MDM**, a different login, an API key or a `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*` variable skips
  server-managed settings, `allowedProviders` included (📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ R1.8 #3, G11). So S5's
  "nobody can turn off all prompts unnoticed" is likely unreachable without MDM (⚠️).
- **Auto memory:** engineers review it and delete it after a suspicious session; residual risk with a
  named owner (D3).
- **Fallback:** switch to `disableAutoMode` if the planted-injection test steers auto mode, a serious
  advisory appears, or an audit finds auto mode touched a protected scope (D1).

**Audit evidence.** Managed settings in git with PR approvals; `/status` and `claude doctor` from
sampled machines (📖 R1.1.18); OTel `claude_code.tool_decision` (`permission_mode`) and
`claude_code.tool.blocked_on_user` (`duration_ms`, rubber-stamping signal) (fields 📖 research 6.6
D1 metrics; thresholds ⚠️). Settings-change audit events on Team: unknown (⚠️ R1.1.12).

**Cost / value.** More prompts than auto mode, partly offset by the read-only allowlist. Compliance
gets one organization policy with evidence instead of personal choices (P3c).

---

## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level

**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Higher risk adds a second, specialised
approver. Incidents use the same path with faster people, not fewer security checks.

| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (it writes state, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release, `CLAUDE.md` | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `.claude/**`, `.mcp.json`, plugin/MCP catalogue; policy violation | 2 distinct humans, at least one platform approver | same path, second approval by path rule or risk stop |
| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b) | layer 7 |
| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | data owner + approver ≠ requester, with an agreement (GĐ-9) | layer 6 |

`CLAUDE.md` is L2, not L3, so that moving shared knowledge into it (D3) stays cheap.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is
  no merge queue (⚠️ R4.6 #1; whether updating drops approvals is open, Options §8).
- **L3 approvals [design]:** a path rule requires 1 platform approval on L3 paths (📖 R3.2.4). Because
  any one code owner satisfies code-owner review (📖 R3.2.7), one platform member could satisfy both
  rules alone (⚠️ inference); a required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5) therefore confirms
  two distinct human approvers. At 2 a.m. this needs the platform on-call plus one other approver.
- **Risk stop [design]:** the deploy job previews prod; on stateful replace/delete, an IAM change or a
  policy violation it stops. A second PR adds `deploy-approvals/<sha>.yaml` with the preview hash; a
  platform approver other than the first approver approves (checked as above); the job continues only
  if the hash matches (Options §1; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8). Preview output is filtered for
  outputs and secrets before it is posted (Options §1; ⚠️ R4.6 #2).
- **Merge approval = deploy approval** only if (⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c): `production`
  allows only `main`; only the reusable deploy workflow (under CODEOWNERS) references it; no ref/SHA
  inputs; no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers; one concurrency group
  per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4).
- **Pulumi:** PRs preview non-prod only, because a prod preview runs PR code with state-write and
  secret access (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). On `main`: prod preview, then `pulumi up` with the
  policy pack, which stops on a mandatory violation (📖 R4.2.2). Prod runs allow no `--skip-preview`
  (📖 R4.1.2) and no targeting, replace, `state`, `import`, `destroy` (⚠️ R4.6 #3, G12). Pulumi Cloud,
  if used: OIDC via `pulumi/auth-actions`, no stored token (📖 R4.1.4).
- **Serverless v4:** `serverless package`; `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI
  because differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2); `serverless deploy --package`
  (📖 R4.4.3); a least-privilege `deploymentRole`, which cannot be removed later and is usable by
  anyone who may operate the stack (📖 R4.4.5), so JIT roles get no stack-operation rights.
- **State:** writable only by deploy roles; readable also by the drift role (layer 7); Pulumi
  secrets via `awskms` on a DIY backend (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #7).
- **k0s [design]:** manifests in the monorepo, applied by CI; no write RBAC for humans or agents in
  prod; read roles exclude logs and exec in namespaces with claim data (mechanism: G1).
- **Incident lane:** label `incident`, on-call approver paged, security checks always run (S10), only
  slow unrelated tests skipped [design].

**Example: Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m.** (Options §6)

1. The incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as the engineer.
3. The on-call approver reviews the diff, and can catch a missing queue change, then approves.
4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.

**Audit evidence.** The PR (diff, approvers, checks); run log and preview artifact, exported because
retention is unverified (⚠️ G7); deploy-role CloudTrail events; all linked by commit SHA and run ID.

**Cost / value.** One approval for routine prod changes, two for risky ones, none in non-prod.
Compliance gets four-eyes enforced by GitHub. Gap: on Team the prod diff is not seen before apply.

## Layer 4 — Supply chain for MCP servers and plugins

**Principle.** MCP servers, plugins and hooks run with the engineer's access (📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.5).
Only reviewed, pinned entries from a catalogue are allowed. The catalogue is the inventory (P4c).
Review takes ≤ 5 working days (S6), or people work around it.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Plugins:** a private marketplace repo with `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (📖 R1.4.1), sources
  pinned to `ref`/`sha` (📖 R1.4.1b, link only). Managed `strictKnownMarketplaces` = Papaya only,
  `blockedMarketplaces`, `enabledPlugins: false` to pull one (📖 R1.4.2), checked before download and
  at session start (📖 R1.4.3). `disableSideloadFlags` rejects `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`,
  `--agents`, `--mcp-config` but not `.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add` (📖 R1.4.2). With
  `allowManagedHooksOnly`, plugin hooks run only for force-enabled plugins (📖 R1.5.4). User mods are
  blocked by the `allowManagedModsOnly` option under `pluginConfigs` → `cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin`
  → `options` (📖 R1.5.6). The version floor covers the plugin-pin fix of 2.1.179 (📖 R6.2.7).
- **MCP:** "approved catalogue" = `allowedMcpServers` + `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true`; without
  the lock users can widen it (📖 R1.3.1, R1.3.4). Match by `serverUrl` or `serverCommand`, never
  `serverName` ("not a security control", 📖 R1.3.3); the argv pins an exact version (⚠️ R6.4.4).
  `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true` (📖 R1.3.7). With MDM, `managed-mcp.json` gives exclusive control;
  it cannot come from server-managed settings (📖 R1.3.2).
- **Review checklist** [design]: publisher; local `stdio` or remote (📖 R6.4.3); what it reads and where
  it sends data, with a supplier-register entry and BAA/DPA status (⚠️ R5.6); no token passthrough
  (📖 R6.4.2); write tools for Slack, Linear, GitHub only where needed (⚠️ R6.5 #6); pinned version,
  reviewer, date.
- **Known gaps:** no per-group targeting in server-managed settings (📖 R1.1.6, R1.4.4); tool
  description changes after approval are not covered (⚠️ research 6.6).

**Audit evidence.** Catalogue file in git (each entry = an approved PR); supplier register; OTel
`claude_code.plugin_installed` / `plugin_loaded` (📖 R1.4.6). MCP tool logging needs
`OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1` (📖 R1.3.8); it stays off until we know whether it logs tool inputs (⚠️).

**Cost / value.** Up to 5 days' wait for a new tool. Compliance gets an asset inventory and supplier
records.

## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening

**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
checks as human code (S10).

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). `GITHUB_TOKEN` "restricted" by default, `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
  deploys may still need a stored credential: a proposed time-boxed exception to S2 = 0 (Q1).
- **Side paths:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard providers reach AWS
  (📖 R4.4.9) outside the GitHub gate (⚠️ R4.4.9); not used for prod (⚠️ R4.6 #6).
- **Pinning:** workflow lockfile (`gh actions-lock`) or full SHA, enforced by the org policy "Require
  actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA"; the lockfile does not pin reusable workflows, so
  the deploy workflow lives in the same repo (📖 R3.5.5).
- **CODEOWNERS** on `.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`,
  `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc` (📖 R3.2.8; list ⚠️ R6.5 #5); CI validates the file, because
  invalid lines are skipped silently (📖 R3.2.7).
- **No privileged triggers with untrusted code** (`pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` + checkout,
  📖 R3.5.4).
- **Agents in CI:** `claude-code-action` with a custom GitHub App limited to Contents, Issues, Pull
  requests (📖 R1.7.8); Anthropic workload identity federation, not a personal OAuth token (📖 R1.7.6);
  `--restricted` and explicit `--tools` (D3; passing it through `claude_args` unverified, ⚠️ research
  6.9.4 Q5); a managed-settings file on the runner, which also guards against mods (📖 R1.5.6; for
  federation auth ⚠️); MCP set fixed by CI because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
  (📖 R1.3.5); never `environment: production` (⚠️ R3.6 #4). Hosted runners give `sudo` (📖 R3.5.1),
  so with `Bash` in `--tools` the runner file is advisory (⚠️ R3.5.1, R3.6 #4).
- **App-opened PRs:** a required check with a pinned source app confirms at least one approval by a
  human who did not trigger the run; counting approvals is not enough, since the app's own approval
  might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3; 📖 R3.2.5).
- **Required checks (S10):** secret scanning, dependency check, SAST (products: G4); IAM Access
  Analyzer `check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1); Pulumi policy packs (📖 R4.2.2).

**Audit evidence.** Workflows and lockfile in git; audit-log events such as
`org.update_actions_secret`, `repo.set_workflow_permission_can_approve_pr`, `repository_ruleset.update`
(📖 R3.3.3, R3.5.6); check results per PR; secrets inventory (S2).

**Cost / value.** One-time migration to OIDC and pinned actions; slower action updates. Compliance
gets S2 and the same guardrails for agent and human code.

## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence

**Principle.** PHI never reaches the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9). Other customer
personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved,
tenant-scoped, time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic (GĐ-14).

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Paths to PHI** (research 1.11.4 lists 17):
  - AWS stores: closed by identity, through `ProdReadMetadata` from phase 1 and the SCP from phase 2
    (layer 1); no Aurora credentials, no prod exec, no `lambda:InvokeFunction` for agent-usable roles
    [design; actions ⚠️ G13];
  - k0s logs/exec and GCP stores (L1, L11, L13): same principle, mechanism open (G1, G3);
  - tickets/chat via MCP, pasted text, internal admin pages, prod AI traces, fixtures, CI logs (L5,
    L8–L10, L12, L14): process and hygiene only;
  - logs redacted at source with raw payloads in a separate log group; alerts carry IDs, not payloads [design].
- **Real-data request** [design]: tenant, purpose, store, window, agreement; approved by the data owner
  and an approver ≠ requester; JIT data-read role, 1 h. Per-tenant scoping through session tags
  (📖 R2.1.8) is unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️).
  - **PHI:** a human reads in a terminal without an agent; the agent gets a redacted summary. This
    narrows GĐ-9 because the agent stays outside PHI scope (research 1.9) and Team is not shown as
    BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Enterprise + BAA only for a separate environment if needed (research 1.9).
  - **Non-PHI personal data:** the agent may read it within the approved request (GĐ-9).
- **Partner-uploaded claim documents (A7b):** never in an agent session raw; reproduce with synthetic
  documents, or de-identify first [design]. The document is PHI and an injection vector (research
  1.11.4 L6).
- **Injection** (these lower frequency; layers 1 and 3 limit impact): Manual by default; the auto-mode
  classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions (📖 R6.3.5). Broad allowed domains such as
  `github.com` are a documented exfiltration path (📖 R6.3.7). The incident session has no edit tools
  and runs outside the repo, but its Bash can still write locally and send data out through excluded
  commands (layer 2); what is at stake is bounded by "no standing write, no PHI read". Shared knowledge
  goes in `CLAUDE.md` under review; auto memory is unprotected unless `--restricted` (📖 R6.3.11, D3).
- **Tenants:** one tenant per data-read grant; a session that read one tenant's data does not post to
  shared places without review (⚠️ R6.5 #8, process). Logical separation in shared accounts is assumed
  (GĐ-3).
- **Non-prod:** no prod copies (S11). A scan of non-prod stores runs at the start of phase 1 (tool:
  G4); a store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule (GĐ-14). Cost: until scanned, that store is
  not part of the free loop.
- **Local stores:** transcripts and memory hold what the agent read (research 1.11.4); set
  `cleanupPeriodDays` (30 in the HIPAA sample, 📖 R5.5.4; what it deletes ⚠️).
- **Cross-border (Vietnam example):** processing data collected in Vietnam on a platform abroad is a
  transfer (📖 R5.4.5); agent flows, including employee names in logs and transcripts, update the
  transfer impact assessment (⚠️ R5.7 #4, needs Papaya legal).

**Audit evidence.** SCP/IAM text as the written access rule for sensitive data (📖 R5.4.3; ⚠️ R5.7 #5);
data-read requests and the data-read role's CloudTrail; planted-injection reports (layer 8); non-prod
scan results (S11).

**Cost / value.** Debugging with redacted and synthetic data; a request for the rare real-data read.
Compliance gets "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM, and a record per exception (S9).

## Layer 7 — Observability, audit, incident response and break-glass

**Principle.** One tamper-evident evidence chain per prod change. One routed alert channel with a
named on-call, approvers included. Unapproved change is detected (drift, reconciliation). Break-glass
is approved before use, time-boxed and reconciled after.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Audit stores:**
  - organization CloudTrail to a log-archive account with integrity validation (📖 R2.6.2, R2.6.4,
    R2.6.5); change records ≥ 6 years; raw-log retention for Papaya's compliance owner (⚠️ R5.7 #2).
    Data events only on PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS (📖 R2.6.3), which makes the archive
    PHI-bearing (⚠️ research 1.11.4 L15). CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers (📖 R2.6.6);
  - GitHub org audit log kept 180 days, so exported (📖 R3.5.6);
  - alerts on `repository_ruleset.update`, `environment.update_protection_rule`,
    `environment.remove_protection_rule`, `environment.delete`, `protected_branch.policy_override`
    (📖 R3.5.6, R3.1.4; selection ⚠️ R3.6 #1). UI changes to the branch policy may leave no event, and a
    deleted `production` environment comes back unprotected (⚠️ R3.1.4): a job compares live settings
    with an expected copy (G8);
  - Aurora SQL is likely invisible to CloudTrail (⚠️ R2.7.1): Database Activity Streams, alerts on
    lost-record events, stream treated as PHI (📖 R2.7.2; Serverless v2 ⚠️);
  - Claude Code OTel without prompt content (layer 2).
- **Change record [design]:** keyed by commit SHA or JIT request ID; links PR, approvals, run ID,
  preview and CloudTrail events. Monthly reconciliation: every prod write event matches a record
  approved before apply (S3). Actor: `onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name plus
  directory lookup (📖 R2.5.1; ⚠️ R2.5.3).
- **Drift [design]:** its own read role, trusted only from a `drift` environment on `main`; it can read
  prod secrets in state, which is noted (⚠️ R4.6 #2). Scheduled `pulumi preview --refresh
  --expect-no-changes` or `pulumi refresh --preview-only` (📖 R4.1.1, R4.3.1, R4.3.2); CloudFormation
  drift detection, explicitly set properties only (📖 R4.4.6). No auto-remediation: it is an unreviewed
  `pulumi up --refresh` (📖 R4.3.2). Each finding gets an actor and a ticket.
- **On-call:** phase 1 delivers only the named approver schedule (primary + backup, 24/7), as decided
  in framing round 1, including a platform approver because L3 needs one (Options §1). Alert routing and
  the rest of on-call follow in phase 2 (tools: G5).
- **Break-glass = JIT fallback** [design unless marked]:

  | Step | Rule |
  |---|---|
  | When | The PR path cannot be used: operation not in IaC and no runbook; GitHub/Actions down; pipeline broken. The approver refuses JIT for anything expressible in IaC while the pipeline works, and records why. |
  | Request | Command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub. |
  | Approval | On-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant. |
  | Grant | `InfraOperator-<service>`, 1 h (📖 R2.1.4). Deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3); ending the portal session does not end role sessions (📖 R2.4.3); an immediate stop needs the revocation SCP (📖 R2.4.4). |
  | Execution | The human types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). |
  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |

  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, `claims-doc-extract`, Actions outage. Run
  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."

  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %). On a breach,
  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
  (D2, ⚠️).

**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail; exported GitHub audit log; change records and monthly
reconciliation (S3, S8 ≤ 30 min); JIT requests, reconciliations, codify PRs; drift tickets; on-call
schedule and approval waits (S7).

**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
incidents, plus detection.

## Layer 8 — Governance and rollout

**Principle.** Every control has an owner, a metric and a review date. Policies are files changed by
PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
attacks.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Owners:** DevSecOps (framework, managed settings, catalogue, metrics); platform team (deploy
  workflows, rulesets, pipelines); Compliance (evidence review, supplier register, Statement of
  Applicability); engineering leads (CODEOWNERS); engineering management (on-call schedule).
- **Policy as code:** managed settings, catalogue, SCPs, trust policies, CODEOWNERS and workflows are
  files under CODEOWNERS; GitHub settings that are not files are compared with an expected copy
  (⚠️ R3.6 #1; G8). Few GitHub admins, reviewed quarterly.
- **Metrics:** S1–S11 exactly as in framing §5; this framework adds the JIT metrics (layer 7) and the
  prompt metrics (layer 2). S2 and S5 have caveats (Q1; layer 2).
- **Rollout** (≈ 90 days, GĐ-12 unconfirmed). Framing round 1 Q8: (1) remove long-lived CI credentials,
  (2) narrow standing prod access, (3) MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list before or with (2).

  | Phase | Days | Items, in order |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | 0–30 | Measure the incident PR lane on one service (first task, Options §9). Non-prod data scan. OIDC for deploy workflows; remove long-lived keys; move laptop deploys (GĐ-10) to CI. Rulesets and CODEOWNERS. `ProdReadMetadata`; start moving secrets to runtime resolution. On-call approver schedule and minimal JIT fallback, **then** remove standing prod write. MCP/plugin catalogue v1. Managed settings baseline. Start verifying the SSM option (Options §7). The last two may slip to phase 2 if the 1–2 person team (GĐ-1) runs short. |
  | 2 | 30–60 | SCP data-plane deny; drift detection; audit-log export, change records, reconciliation; Aurora activity streams; JIT reconciliation job; alert routing and the rest of on-call. |
  | 3 | 60–90 | Planted-injection test on the real configuration (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.5; ⚠️ R6.5 #12); auto-mode non-prod environment (D1 c); separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions; first ISO evidence pack; 90-day review of D1–D3. |

- **Exceptions:** a ticket with owner, reason and expiry.
- **Standards mapping** (⚠️ R5.6; HIPAA and Vietnam text 📖 R5.2, R5.4; ISO IDs recalled, not read,
  ⚠️ R5.1):

  | Layers | ISO 27001:2022 Annex A (⚠️) | HIPAA Security Rule | Vietnam example |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1, 6 access | 5.15–5.18, 8.2, 8.3, 8.5 | 164.312(a)(2)(i); 164.308(a)(3)–(4) | Decree 356 Art. 4(2) |
  | 3, 5 change | 8.32, 8.31, 8.25, 5.3 | 164.312(c); 164.316(b) | — |
  | 7 logging, break-glass | 8.15, 8.16, 5.28 | 164.312(b); 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D); 164.312(a)(2)(ii) (mapping ⚠️ R5.7 #3) | Law 91 Art. 23 (72 h notice) |
  | 4 suppliers | 5.19–5.23 | 164.308(b), 164.314(a) | Law 91 Art. 20 |

  "A named human approves" is Papaya's chosen way to meet these controls, not a literal requirement
  (⚠️ R5.7 #1).
- **Out of scope:** security of the production AI agents (A7a); noted as a follow-up.

**Audit evidence.** Git history of policy files; monthly metrics; 90-day review minutes; exception
register; planted-injection reports.

**Cost / value.** Steady, small overhead for DevSecOps and platform. Compliance gets a managed system
with owners and review dates.

-**Cross-cutting rules** (from the owner's balance principle, `work/02-research.md` 6.8):

-   the docs call server-managed settings "a client-side control, not a security boundary"

### Roles

-App with pull-request write might approve PRs; whether such an approval counts is unknown
-(⚠️ R3.7 A3), so the gate relies on a check that requires a human approver (layer 5). This is a
-process rule with residual risk. No detection mechanism was found in the researched sources; the
-org audit log's `actor_is_agent` field is a candidate whose meaning is undocumented (⚠️ R3.5.6).
## Layer 1 — Identity and access
-**Principle**
+**Principle.** Every action traces to one named human. Nobody holds standing prod write: prod is
+written by the pipeline role, or in the fallback by an approved, time-boxed grant. Prod reads default
+to metadata. No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.
-- Every action traces to one named human.
-- Nobody holds standing write access to production. Production is written by the pipeline role,
-  or, in the fallback, by an approved, time-boxed human grant.
-- Production reads default to metadata. Reads of stores that hold customer data are blocked by a
-  guardrail that member-account identities cannot edit.
-- No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.
**On Papaya's stack**
-- **The human's access is the agent's access.** On a laptop the agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO
-  cache, and one portal session reaches every role assigned to the engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2). A
-  separate "agent" permission set therefore does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is
-  what the **engineer** holds.
-- **AWS IAM Identity Center permission sets** (📖 R2.1.1):
-  - `ProdReadMetadata`: config, metrics and redacted log groups in prod; no data-plane read on
-    stores holding claim data (from phase 1, before the SCP in phase 2); session duration 1 h, the
-    minimum (📖 R2.1.4). Caveat: function configuration can contain secrets, because values that
-    Serverless resolves may sit in Lambda environment variables in plain text (⚠️ R4.4.7). Phase 1
-    moves secrets to runtime resolution (⚠️ R4.6 #7); until a service is moved, its configuration
-    read is excluded and the agent reads timeout/memory from the IaC code. Cost: a less exact view
-    of live state for those services.
-  - `NonProdDeveloper`: broad rights in non-prod accounts only.
-  - **No standing prod-write permission set.**
-  - `InfraOperator-<service>`: assigned only by the JIT flow (layer 7). Tooling: a partner product,
-    the TEAM sample, or a small flow on `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment`
-- **Guardrails in the prod OU (SCPs)**, which cap member-account principals (📖 R2.3.1, R2.3.2) [design]:
-  - deny data-plane reads on stores holding claim data except application roles and the approved
-    data-read role, selected by `aws:PrincipalArn` (key 📖 R2.3.8; pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4). Example
-    actions, incomplete and not checked against the IAM reference (⚠️ research 1.11.4, G13):
-    `s3:GetObject` on the claim-documents bucket, `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`;
-  - deny `lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` and `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` (action names
-    ⚠️ R4.6 #3) except the CloudFormation `deploymentRole` and the named JIT roles, to close
-    `serverless deploy function`, which changes config outside CloudFormation (📖 R4.4.4; SCP or IAM
-    not chosen);
-  - the role that deploys SCPs works in the management account, where no SCP applies (📖 R2.3.2):
-    it is the most sensitive deploy role and gets its own L3 path rule;
-  - a pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:userId` (📖 R2.4.4);
-  - protect the organization trail and log archive (📖 R2.6.2).
-  Limits: 10 SCPs per target, 10,240 characters each; nothing applies to the management account
-- **Sessions and MFA:** set the access-portal session length on purpose; the IdP session can
-  silently extend it (📖 R2.1.5, R2.1.6). MFA is managed in the external IdP if one is used (📖 R2.1.7).
-- **CI → AWS:** GitHub OIDC, no stored keys (📖 R3.4.1). The prod deploy role trusts only tokens
-  from the `production` environment of Papaya's monorepo, in the repo's `sub` format (📖 R3.4.3,
-  R3.4.4; the immutable format is assumed, ⚠️ R3.7 A2). Preferably the `sub` is customised to also
-  include the reusable deploy workflow's `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; availability on Team ⚠️, G10).
-  Non-prod roles trust non-prod environments or `pull_request` (⚠️ R4.6 #2).
-- **CI → GCP:** Workload Identity Federation with an attribute condition on Papaya's GitHub
-  organization, which Google requires (📖 R3.4.5b).
-- **GCP, k0s and Firebase for humans:** same principles; mechanisms not researched (G1–G3). Today
-  engineers reach k0s with kubeconfigs and no SSO (GĐ-4, unconfirmed). Interim rule: no admin
-  kubeconfig and no GCP owner role on laptops; prod deploys to k0s and Firebase run only from CI.
-  Until G1/G2 are solved, those CI jobs may still need a stored kubeconfig or token: a time-boxed
-  exception to S2, with an owner, in the exception register (layer 8). Firebase is not on the GCP
-  BAA list, so Firebase Hosting must hold no PHI (📖 R5.5.3).
+- **The engineer's access is the agent's access.** The agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and
+  one portal session reaches every role assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2). A separate
+  "agent" permission set does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is what the **engineer**
+  holds.
+- **Process rules** that follow from this (owner accepted them as process controls, D2, D3):
+  - the JIT terminal and the real-data terminal run no agent, though the grant is reachable from the
+    same laptop;
+  - the incident-analysis session is meant to use only read-only roles;
+  - an agent does not approve PRs. GitHub blocks self-approval only. The auto-mode default block list
+    names "approving Claude's own pull request", not approving someone else's (📖 R6.3.3), and it
+    applies only in auto mode. No detection was found (⚠️; `actor_is_agent` in the audit log has no
+    documented meaning, R3.5.6).
+- **IAM Identity Center permission sets** (📖 R2.1.1) [design names]:
+  - `ProdReadMetadata`: metrics, redacted log groups, configuration; no data-plane read on claim
+    stores; 1 h session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). Lambda configuration can hold secrets resolved by
+    Serverless in plain text (⚠️ R4.4.7), so configuration reads are allowed per service only after
+    its secrets move to runtime resolution (⚠️ R4.6 #7). Cost: until then the agent reads

+  - `NonProdDeveloper`: broad, non-prod accounts only;
+  - `InfraOperator-<service>`: assigned only by the JIT flow (layer 7), via a partner product, the
+    TEAM sample or a small flow on `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment`
+  - no standing prod-write permission set.
+- **SCPs on the prod OU** [design] (SCPs cap member-account principals, 📖 R2.3.1, R2.3.2):
+  - deny data-plane reads on claim stores except application roles and the approved data-read role,
+    by `aws:PrincipalArn` (📖 R2.3.8; pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4). Actions, e.g. `s3:GetObject`,
+    `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`, are incomplete and unchecked (⚠️ G13);

+    (📖 R4.4.4), and needs `deploymentRole` set on every Serverless stack (📖 R4.4.5);
+  - a pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:userId` (📖 R2.4.4); protect the org trail (📖 R2.6.2).
+  - Limits: 10 SCPs per target, 10,240 characters; no SCP applies to the management account
+    (📖 R2.3.2, R2.3.4), so whatever deploys SCPs there is the most sensitive role (L3 path).
+- **Sessions/MFA:** portal session length set on purpose; an IdP session can extend it silently
+  (📖 R2.1.5, R2.1.6). MFA lives in the external IdP if one is used (📖 R2.1.7).
+- **CI → AWS:** GitHub OIDC, no stored keys (📖 R3.4.1). The prod role trusts only the `production`

+  ⚠️ R3.7 A2), ideally customised with the deploy workflow's `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
+- **CI → GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization, which Google
+  requires (📖 R3.4.5b).
+- **k0s, GCP and Firebase for humans:** same principles; mechanisms not researched (G1–G3). Today
+  k0s is reached with kubeconfigs, no SSO (GĐ-4, unconfirmed). Interim: no admin kubeconfig and no GCP
+  owner role on laptops; prod deploys only from CI. Firebase is not on the GCP BAA list (📖 R5.5.3), so
+  Firebase Hosting must hold no PHI (⚠️ R5.7 #7).
-**Audit evidence**
+**Audit evidence.** Identity Center assignment export (S1); CloudTrail `CreateAccountAssignment` /
+`DeleteAccountAssignment` per grant (📖 R2.4.2), linked to its approval by request ID [design]; SCPs
+and trust policies as Pulumi code; IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on policy PRs
+(📖 R2.8.1); quarterly access review of permission sets and GitHub admins.
-- Export of Identity Center assignments: no standing prod-write assignment (S1).
-- CloudTrail `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment` per JIT grant (📖 R2.4.2), linked
-  to the approval record by request ID [design].
-- SCPs and trust policies as Pulumi code: version history = change history.
-- IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on every PR that changes a policy (📖 R2.8.1).

+**Cost / value.** Engineers lose standing prod write, keep fast prod reads and a free non-prod loop.
+Compliance gets least privilege that is enforced.
-**Cost / value.** Engineers lose standing prod write; they keep fast prod reads and a free non-prod
-loop. Compliance gets least privilege that is enforced, not promised.
## Layer 2 — Agent runtime controls
-**Principle**
+**Principle.** Agent-side controls are hygiene, not the boundary. They are central, versioned in git
+and the same for everyone. Defaults are safe; overrides are measured. The session that reads
+untrusted content holds as little power as possible (📖 R6.1.2).
-- Agent-side controls are hygiene: they cut mistakes; they are not the boundary (📖 R1.1.7, R1.1.8).
-- They are set centrally, the same for everyone, and versioned in git.
-- Safe defaults with a measured escape hatch. A default that people keep overriding is replaced,
-  not defended.
-- The session that reads untrusted content should hold as little power as possible (📖 R6.1.2).
**On Papaya's stack**
-- **Delivery:** server-managed settings from the claude.ai admin console (available on Team,
-  📖 R1.1.5) for all laptops. Where MDM exists, also an endpoint `managed-settings.json`, protected
-  at OS level, though a local admin can still edit it (📖 R1.1.3, R1.1.8). MDM is unknown, so both
-  paths are prepared (R1.9).
-- **Baseline keys** (template: Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json`, 📖 R5.5.4):
+- **Delivery:** server-managed settings (available on Team, 📖 R1.1.5) for all laptops. With MDM, also
+  an endpoint file; by default one managed source supplies most keys, so the two must carry the same
+  keys or use `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"` (📖 R1.1.3, R1.1.4). MDM is unknown; both are prepared.
+- **Baseline** (template: Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json`, 📖 R5.5.4). All keys 📖 at the row cited:

## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level
-**Principle**
+**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
+reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
+The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Higher risk adds a second, specialised
+approver. Incidents use the same path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
-- The level is set by the damage a change can do, not by who asks.

-  change that will be applied and is a named human who is not the author. (On GitHub Team the prod
-  diff itself is not seen before apply, ⚠️ R4.6 #1.)
-- Higher risk adds a specialised second approver, not a different path.
-- An incident uses the same path with faster people, not fewer security checks.

+**Principle.** PHI never reaches the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9). Other customer
+personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
+by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved,
+tenant-scoped, time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
+from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic (GĐ-14).

-  phase 1 by the permission set). k0s logs and exec and GCP stores (research 1.11.4 L1, L11, L13)

  ### MEDIUM
  
  **M1. Layer 2, đoạn "Trade-off on AWS credentials": câu "Accepted because the engineer holds no prod write and no PHI read" đúng với quyền thường trực, nhưng sai trong lúc có cửa sổ JIT hoặc data-read.**
  - Layer 1 tự thừa nhận "the grant is reachable from the same laptop".
  - `aws`, `pulumi` và `serverless` là `excludedCommands` nên chạy với full network (📖 R1.6.4).
  - Vì vậy, trong lúc có grant, một session agent khác trên cùng laptop dùng được role JIT hoặc data-read và gửi dữ liệu ra ngoài allowlist.
  - Principle của Layer 6 ("PHI never reaches the coding agent") trong cửa sổ PHI-read thực chất chỉ dựa vào quy trình.
  - Sửa: đổi thành "no **standing** prod write and no **standing** PHI read" như Layer 6 đang viết. Thêm một câu: "during a JIT or data-read window this rests on the process rule in layer 1 (D2)". Ở Layer 6 PHI bullet, thêm "process rule, see layer 1".
  
  **M2. Bảng L0–L3 ở Layer 3: L3-JIT chỉ cần 1 người duyệt ("on-call approver ≠ requester"), trong khi L3 cần "2 distinct humans, at least one platform approver".**
  - Qua break-glass, một thay đổi IAM, SCP hoặc stateful lại có ít người duyệt hơn đường thường.
  - Điều này mâu thuẫn với Principle của chính Layer 3: "Incidents use the same path with faster people, not fewer security checks".
  - Sửa: hoặc quy định JIT chạm vào lớp thay đổi L3 thì cần thêm platform approver, hoặc ghi rõ đây là ngoại lệ có chủ ý (kèm lý do) trong "Where the design falls short".
  
  **M3. Layer 3, bullet "Risk stop [design]": cơ chế dừng vì "policy violation" không khớp với cách Pulumi hoạt động.**
  - Hiện tại job dừng khi gặp "a policy violation", rồi chạy tiếp nếu có PR thứ hai và hash khớp.
  - Nhưng vi phạm policy mức `mandatory` luôn chặn `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2), dù có file approval hay không.
  - Sửa: tách ra hai trường hợp. Vi phạm `advisory` thì cần duyệt lần hai. Vi phạm `mandatory` thì phải sửa code, hoặc đổi policy pack qua một PR L3.
  
  **M4. Làn sự cố (Roles, Layer 3 "Incident lane"): framework bỏ qua một trade-off chưa giải mà Options §1 và §7 đã nêu.**
  - Muốn on-call approver duyệt được lúc 2 giờ sáng thì người đó phải là code owner của mọi path deploy (R3.2.7). Khi đó review thường ngày mất chuyên môn theo domain.
  - Options §7 ghi rõ "chưa có cách giải được kiểm chứng".
  - Nếu không nhắc điều này, câu "approval wait ≤ 15 min" (S7) nghe như đã khả thi.
  - Sửa: thêm một dòng vào "Where the design falls short" hoặc vào Layer 3, ghi trade-off này là open item và trỏ về Options §1 và §8.
  
  **M5. Bảng Layer 3, hàng L1: "`pulumi preview` on non-prod (it writes state, 📖 R4.3.3)" nói quá mức nguồn.**
  - R4.3.3 chỉ nói backend S3 cần quyền `PutObject`/`DeleteObject` "across the full stack lifecycle, including preview".
  - R4.6 #2 ghi rõ preview có ghi gì (ví dụ chỉ `locks/`) hay không là ⚠️ chưa kiểm.
  - Sửa: "(needs state-write permission, 📖 R4.3.3)".
  
  **M6. Mục 1, bảng "Compliance gets": hai câu được nói như tuyệt đối, trong khi chỗ khác của framework đã thừa nhận giới hạn.**
  - Câu "approved before apply by a named human ≠ author (GĐ-8, GĐ-11), enforced in GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent":
    - GĐ-11 tính cả agent là "người làm".
    - Layer 1 thừa nhận "an agent does not approve PRs" chỉ là process rule, và không phát hiện được: agent của engineer B có thể duyệt bằng login của B.
  - Câu "no long-lived CI keys (S2)":
    - Mâu thuẫn với Layer 5 và Q1, nơi đề xuất ngoại lệ S2 cho k0s và Firebase.
  - Sửa: thêm vào "Where the design falls short" một dòng "Approval by a human, not by an agent using that human's login, is a process rule (layer 1)". Đổi S2 thành "S2 (exception pending Q1)".
  
  **M7. Tham chiếu "Q-n" bị trùng nghĩa.**
  - Legend định nghĩa Q-n là câu hỏi owner ở cuối tài liệu.
  - Nhưng Layer 2 viết "owner Q4" (ý là research 6.9.4 Q4), "D3, owner Q1–Q2" (6.9.4 Q1–Q2), "owner Q5" (6.9.4 Q5). Mục 1 viết "Options §9 Q2". Layer 8 viết "Q8" (framing vòng 1).

  - Sửa: dùng tiền tố rõ ràng, ví dụ "R6.9.4 Q4", "framing Q8", "Options Q2".

  - Thực ra `onFailure` là tuỳ chọn của hook. 2.1.295 là phiên bản tối thiểu để tuỳ chọn đó hoạt động.
  - Sửa: "≥ 2.1.295, the first version with hook `onFailure: "block"` (R1.5.2)".
  
  **M9. Thiếu bước trong rollout: chưa có dòng nào lên lịch "logs redacted at source, raw payloads in a separate log group".**
  - Việc này ở Layer 6 đang là [design].
  - Nhưng `ProdReadMetadata` (phase 1) cấp quyền đọc "redacted log groups", và ví dụ 2 giờ sáng đọc "redacted logs".
  - Nếu không làm việc redaction, hoặc agent không có log nào để đọc, hoặc phải mở quyền đọc log thô (trái với PHI decision).
  - Sửa: thêm "log redaction at source for services in scope" vào phase 1 hoặc 2. Đồng thời ghi rõ: cho tới khi một service được redact, `ProdReadMetadata` chỉ đọc metrics của service đó, giống cách đang làm với configuration.

  - **L1.** Layer 7: "stream treated as PHI (📖 R2.7.2)". Ý "treat as PHI" nằm ở R2.7.3 và là ⚠️ inference. Sửa: "(⚠️ R2.7.3)".
  - **L2.** Legend định nghĩa "⚠️ Rx.y" chỉ cho các mục inference (1.8, 2.9…). Nhưng tài liệu cũng dùng ⚠️ cho các dòng hỗn hợp ✅/⚠️ (R1.11.1.11, R2.4.2, R2.5.3, R2.7.1, R3.1.4, R3.3.4, R3.5.1, R4.4.7, R4.4.9). Sửa legend: "…or the ⚠️ part of a mixed row".
  - **L3.** Layer 5: "`GITHUB_TOKEN` "restricted" by default" có thể bị hiểu là mặc định của GitHub. R3.5.3 nói mặc định có thể là permissive hoặc restricted. Sửa: "set the org default to "restricted"".
  - **L4.** Danh sách path L3 (`.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `.claude/**`, `.mcp.json`) chưa phân loại `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, `.claude.json`, `CLAUDE.local.md`. Các path này có trong danh sách CODEOWNERS ở Layer 5. Riêng `.husky/` chạy code trên máy dev. Nên nói rõ chúng là L2 hay L3.
  - **L5.** Hàng sandbox ở Layer 2: `sandbox.credentials` / `filesystem.denyRead` được cite R1.6.3, nhưng tên key nằm ở R1.6.4.

  - **L7.** Hai chỗ lệch nhỏ với GĐ:
    - "move laptop deploys (GĐ-10)" chưa ghi GĐ-10 là giả định chưa xác nhận, trong khi framing §6 có ghi.
    - GĐ-14 là "synthetic **hoặc đã che**", còn framework chỉ viết "synthetic".

  - **L10.** Bảng standards mapping:
    - "Law 91 Art. 23 (72 h notice)" ở hàng logging/break-glass không có trong mapping của R5.6. Nội dung có ở R5.4.6 ✅, nhưng việc map là mới. Nên ghi đây là mapping của chính tài liệu này.

Không có tên tính năng nào bị bịa.

Đủ 8 layer, mỗi layer đều có Principle, On Papaya's stack, Audit evidence và Cost/value. Không có secret, ID thật hay dữ liệu cá nhân. Toàn bộ bằng tiếng Anh. Không có finding HIGH. - Vì vậy, trong lúc có grant, một session agent khác trên cùng laptop dùng được role JIT hoặc data-read và gửi dữ liệu ra ngoài allowlist.
